newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah soft but off lows in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah soft but off lows in thin trade.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was hovering around the 3,000 level against the dollar in thin late trading on Monday after briefly falling to 3,005, dealers said.
They said the rupiah fell through the 3,000 barrier at midday before recovering to 2,970/80 at 0935 GMT.
Dealers said dollar buying interest was mainly from local corporates while offshore took profits in dollars.
Saleh Aziz, treasury manager of PT Bank Export-Import Indonesia, said the dollar appeared to be capped at the 3,000 level but warned of corporates doing aggressive hedging now.
"If the rupiah can fall by 300 rupiah, it can also rise easily by the same extent. If that happens, those corporates are going to get burnt twice," Aziz said.
He added offshore investors were looking for good entry levels into Indonesia because of attractive yields.
"But their interests are put on hold because of sustained local appetite for dollars," he added.
Dealers said liquidity was tight which helped limit further rises in the dollar. Overnight rupiah closed at 100 percent after falling to 30 percent earlier.
Aziz said there was a sharp difference between the short- and the long-term rates, suggesting that investors expected the high rates would be temporary.
Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,965/75 and 2,925/30, respectively. Overnight swap was at 3/4 and tom/next at 7.25/7.50. One-week swap was at 30.0/40.0 points.
One-month swap was at 85/95, two at 115/140, three at 165/170 and six at 240/245 points.
One-month interbank rates were at 40.0/50.0, two, three and six were all at 30.0/40.0 percent.
"There are no fundamentals anymore. It's regardless what you think about fundamentals in the long-term," one market analyst with a U.S. investment bank in Singapore said.

"Everyone believes that in the short-term the rupiah could weaken further to the 3,100 level. I would say based on market sentiment it's going to trade there even though they believe that the fundamentals are strong," the analyst said.
The U.S. analyst said the weakening of the rupiah also resulted from the perception that the rupiah should adjust to some extent to preserve its competitiveness.
"The situation will definitely die down. It's a queston of whether it's within one month or a few months. People are waiting for some stability before they come in again," he said.
Dealers said corporate dollar buying was mainly responsible for the rupiah weakening.
"There is not much trading in the market because of ongoing jitters. But we saw some corporate buying with selling seen mainly from offshore," one local bank dealer said.
"If local corporates could stay calm, I think we could see some quick recovery in the rupiah," the dealer said.

A poll conducted by Reuters forecast the rupiah in a wide range between 3,100.00 and 2,510.00 at the end of the year, but the average came in at 2,785.00, over 10 percent lower, in rupiah terms, than last month's forecast.
"Volume is thin. Previously people were trading in (lots of) 10 (million dollars). Now trade volume has shrunk to one or two and sometimes five," one U.S. bank dealer said.
